_comment: Travel speeds and terrain costs. These are the softest numbers in the whole
project: George R. R. Martin never publishes a rate table, so every figure
here is inferred from journeys described in the text plus real medieval
logistics. They live in config precisely because they are meant to be argued
with — edit, then re-run pipeline/07_validate_routing.py to see the effect on
milesPerDay is a sustained daily march on maintained road, not a sprint.
offRoadPenalty multiplies the terrain cost of every non-road land cell.

foot.label: On foot
foot.note: A party on foot makes about 20 miles a day. An army dragging a baggage train makes rather less, and the Golden Company would tell you so.

horse.label: On horseback
horse.note: A sustainable daily march for a mounted party. A courier riding post with remounts covers two or three times this and ruins horses doing it.

carriage.label: By wheelhouse
carriage.note: Wheeled transport is road-bound and slow. Robert's wheelhouse — forty feet long, drawn by dozens of carthorses — held the royal progress to a crawl and could not leave the kingsroad at all.

dragon.label: By dragon
dragon.note: Flies a straight line over any terrain or sea. 500 miles a day is the fan-consensus sustained pace inferred from flight times in the text; a dragon in haste does far better over short distances.

ship.label: By ship
ship.note: Coast-hugging sail at roughly 5 knots averaged across a full day, allowing for nights at anchor and contrary winds. A swift galley in good weather does better.
